items.title: Cause-Condition-Result Establishment Opens, and How Anything Arises

items.zh: 云何因緣果建立？謂略說有四種。一、由相故；二、由依處故；三、由差別故；四、由建立故。因等相者，謂若由此為先，此為建立。此和合故，彼法生，或得、或成、或辦、或用，說此為彼因。
items.en: Further, how is cause-condition-result establishment to be understood? Stated briefly, there are four gateways: first, through their marks; second, through their loci; third, through their differences; fourth, through their establishment. As for the marks of cause and the rest: whenever, by taking this as prior, this as what establishes, and this as what conjoins, some given thing arises — or is attained, or is accomplished, or is completed, or comes into use — this prior thing is said to be the cause of that.

items.zh: 問：以誰為先？誰為建立？誰和合故？何法生耶？答：自種子為先。除種子依，所餘若有色、若無色依及業為建立。助伴、所緣為和合故。隨其所應，欲繫、色繫、無色繫及不繫諸法生。
items.en: Question: what is taken as prior? What establishes? By conjoining with what? What thing arises? Answer: one's own seed is taken as prior. Apart from the support that is the seed itself, whatever remaining support there may be — whether material or immaterial — together with karma, serve as what establishes. An accompanying mental factor and an object serve as what conjoins. Accordingly, phenomena bound to the desire realm, the form realm, the formless realm, or unbound to any of the three, arise.

items.title: How Liberation Itself Is Attained: Internal and External Conditions

items.zh: 問：以誰為先？誰為建立？誰和合故？得何法耶？答：聲聞、獨覺、如來種性為先。內分力為建立。外分力為和合故。證得煩惱離繫涅槃。
items.en: Question: what is taken as prior? What establishes? By conjoining with what? What thing is attained? Answer: the uncontaminated lineage of the śrāvaka, the pratyekabuddha, or the Tathāgata is taken as prior. An inward-facing power serves as what establishes. An outward-facing power serves as what conjoins. Freedom from the bonds of affliction and the realisation of nirvāṇa are thereby attained.

items.zh: 內分力者，謂如理作意、少欲知足等內分善法，及得人身、生在聖處、諸根無缺、無事業障、於其善處深生淨信，如是等法名內分力。
items.en: As for the inward-facing power: it is sound reasoning attention, contentment with little and knowing what is enough, and other such inwardly-directed wholesome qualities, together with having obtained a human body, having been born in a noble region, having faculties free of any deficiency, being free of any karmic obstruction from past deeds, and having deep, pure faith in that noble domain. Qualities of this kind are called the inward-facing power.

items.zh: 外分力者，謂諸佛興世、宣說妙法、教法猶存、住正法者隨順而轉、具悲信者以為施主，如是等法名外分力。
items.en: As for the outward-facing power: it is buddhas arising in the world, the sublime Dharma being proclaimed, the teaching still remaining, those who abide in the true Dharma transmitting it in accordance with it, and those endowed with compassion and faith serving as benefactors. Qualities of this kind are called the outward-facing power.

items.title: How a Teaching Is Established: Thesis, Reason, Example

items.zh: 問：以誰為先？誰為建立？誰和合故？何法成耶？答：所知勝解、愛樂為先。宗、因、譬喻為建立。不相違眾、善敵論者為和合故。所立義成。
items.en: Question: what is taken as prior? What establishes? By conjoining with what? What thing is established? Answer: firm conviction in, and genuine delight in, what is to be known are taken as prior. Thesis, reason, and example serve as what establishes. An assembly free of contrary bias, together with a worthy opponent skilled in debate, serve as what conjoins. The meaning to be established is thereby established.

items.title: How a Craft Is Completed, and How a Life Is Sustained

items.zh: 問：以誰為先？誰為建立？誰和合故？何法辦耶？答：工巧智為先。隨彼勤劬為建立。工巧業處眾具為和合故。工巧業處辦。又
items.en: Question: what is taken as prior? What establishes? By conjoining with what? What thing is completed? Answer: skilful knowledge of a craft is taken as prior. Diligent effort in accordance with it serves as what establishes. The various tools and materials proper to that craft serve as what conjoins. The craft is thereby completed.

items.zh: 愛為先。由食住者依止為建立。四食為和合故。受生有情安住充辦。
items.en: Further: attachment to renewed existence is taken as prior. The reliance of one who is sustained by food serves as what establishes. The four kinds of food serve as what conjoins. A being taking rebirth is thereby sustained and brought to fulfilment.

items.title: How a Thing Functions — Sense-Faculties and the Four Elements

items.zh: 問：以誰為先？誰為建立？誰和合故？何法用耶？答：即自種子為先。即此生為建立。即此生緣為和合故。自業諸法作用可知。
items.en: Question: what is taken as prior? What establishes? By conjoining with what? What is put to use? Answer: precisely one's own seed is taken as prior. This very arising serves as what establishes. Precisely the conditions for this arising serve as what conjoins. The proper function of each thing may thus be known.

items.zh: 何等名為自業作用？謂眼以見為業，如是餘根各自業用應知。又地能持，水能爛，火能燒，風能燥，如是等類，當知外分自業差別。
items.en: What, then, is meant by a thing's proper function? The eye has seeing as its function; so too should the remaining faculties each be understood to have their own proper function. Further, earth has the function of holding things together, water of causing them to dissolve, fire of burning, and wind of drying — differences of this kind should be understood as the proper functions belonging to external, insentient things.

items.title: The Second Gateway: Fifteen Loci of Cause, Condition, and Result

items.zh: 因等依處者，謂十五種。一、語，二、領受，三、習氣，四、有潤種子，五、無間滅，六、境界，七、根，八、作用，九、士用，十、真實見，十一、隨順，十二、差別功能，十三、和合，十四、障礙，十五、無障礙。
items.en: As for the loci of cause and the rest: they are fifteen in number. First, language. Second, sensation. Third, habitual imprint. Fourth, the moistened seed. Fifth, uninterrupted cessation. Sixth, an object. Seventh, a faculty. Eighth, function. Ninth, human effort. Tenth, genuine insight. Eleventh, conformity. Twelfth, differentiated capacity. Thirteenth, conjunction. Fourteenth, obstruction. Fifteenth, absence of obstruction.

items.title: The Third Gateway: Ten Causes, Four Conditions, Five Results

items.zh: 因等差別者，謂十因、四緣、五果。十因者，一、隨說因，二、觀待因，三、牽引因，四、生起因，五、攝受因，六、引發因，七、定異因，八、同事因，九、相違因，十、不相違因。
items.en: As for the differences among cause and the rest: they comprise ten causes, four conditions, and five results. The ten causes are: first, the cause of designation; second, the cause of correlation; third, the cause of impelling; fourth, the cause of generation; fifth, the cause of inclusion; sixth, the cause of drawing-forth; seventh, the cause of fixed distinction; eighth, the cause of concomitant action; ninth, the cause of opposition; tenth, the cause of non-opposition.

items.zh: 四緣者，一、因緣，二、等無間緣，三、所緣緣，四、增上緣。五果者，一、異熟果，二、等流果，三、離繫果，四、士用果，五、增上果。
items.en: The four conditions are: first, the causal condition; second, the condition of uninterrupted equivalence; third, the object condition; fourth, the dominant condition. The five results are: first, the ripened result; second, the result of equal outflow; third, the result of release from bondage; fourth, the result of human effort; fifth, the dominant result.

items.title: Establishing the Ten Causes: the Cause of Designation

items.zh: 因等建立者，謂依語因依處，施設隨說因。所以者何？由於欲界繫法，色、無色界繫法，及不繫法，施設名為先故想轉，想為先故語轉，由語故，隨見、聞、覺、知起諸言說。是故依語依處，施設隨說因。
items.en: As for the establishment of cause and the rest: it is with reference to the locus of language that the cause of designation is set forth. Why is this? Because, with respect to phenomena bound to the desire realm, phenomena bound to the form or formless realms, and phenomena unbound to any of the three, a name is designated first, and thought proceeds from it; thought comes first, and speech proceeds from it; and by means of speech, all manner of verbal expression arises in accordance with what is seen, heard, sensed, or known. It is for this reason that, with reference to the locus of language, the cause of designation is set forth.

items.title: The Cause of Correlation: Seeking Pleasure, Fleeing Pain

items.zh: 依領受因依處，施設觀待因。所以者何？由諸有情諸有欲求欲繫樂者，彼觀待此，於諸欲具，或為求得、或為積集、或為受用。諸有欲求色無色繫樂者，彼觀待此，於彼諸緣，或為求得、或為受用。諸有欲求不繫樂者，彼觀待此，於彼諸緣、或為求得、或為受用。
items.en: It is with reference to the locus of sensation that the cause of correlation is set forth. Why is this? Because, among beings who desire and seek pleasure bound to the desire realm, correlated against that pleasure, they either seek to obtain, or to accumulate, or to make use of the requisites of desire. Among those who desire and seek pleasure bound to the form or formless realms, correlated against that pleasure, they either seek to obtain or to make use of its conditions. Among those who desire and seek pleasure unbound to any of the three realms, correlated against that pleasure, they either seek to obtain or to make use of its conditions.

items.zh: 諸有不欲苦者，彼觀待此，於彼生緣、於彼斷緣，或為遠離、或為求得、或為受用。是故依領受依處，施設觀待因。
items.en: Among those who do not wish for suffering, correlated against that wish, with respect to the conditions that give rise to suffering and the conditions that end it, they either seek to be free of it, or to obtain its cessation, or to make use of that cessation. It is for this reason that, with reference to the locus of sensation, the cause of correlation is set forth.

items.title: The Cause of Impelling: How Karma Draws a Rebirth

items.zh: 依習氣因依處，施設牽引因。所以者何？由淨不淨業熏習三界諸行，於愛不愛趣中牽引愛不愛自體。又即由此增上力故，外物盛衰。是故依諸行淨不淨業習氣依處，施設牽引因。
items.en: It is with reference to the locus of habitual imprint that the cause of impelling is set forth. Why is this? Because pure and impure karma perfumes the formations of the three realms, and thereby impels a desirable or undesirable body of one's own within a desirable or undesirable destiny. Further, by this same dominant force, the external material world itself flourishes or declines. It is for this reason that, with reference to the locus of the habitual imprint left by the pure and impure karma of the formations, the cause of impelling is set forth.

blocks.text: The eighth and last aspect of the realms is **cause, condition, and result** (因緣果). It is a short treatise on causation, and it introduces a scheme distinctive to this text: **ten causes** (十因), alongside the familiar four conditions and five results. Over the next two days the treatise defines each cause by its "locus" (依處), the place in experience where it can be seen working. Today: how anything arises, the fifteen loci, and the first three causes.

Cause-condition-result is presented through four gateways: marks, loci, differences, and establishment. The marks ask five questions about anything that comes to be: what is prior, what establishes, what conjoins, what arises, and so on. The answer for any phenomenon: "One's own seed is taken as prior"; the other supports and karma establish it; its accompanying factors and its object conjoin with it. It is the four conditions of Day 19, phrased as a process.

The same pattern applies to liberation. It needs an inner power and an outer one. The inner power includes having obtained a human body. Master Cháng Bǎi: "Hell is too painful, the desire heavens too pleasant, form-realm gods too proud"; humans excel in pure conduct, memory, and courage. It also includes being "free of karmic obstruction"; Venerable Miào Jìng adds Kuījī's second reading, not being hindered by busy "Dharma work" that crowds out the path itself. The outer power is the appearance of a Buddha and the teaching.

subs.head: How a teaching is established; how crafts and lives work

blocks.text: A thesis is established by thesis, reason, and example. Master Cháng Bǎi notes that this three-membered form is Dignāga's reform of the older five-membered syllogism, which he judged repetitive. Crafts are completed by skill and tools; life is sustained by food; the senses and elements each function by their own capacity.

Causes and conditions show themselves in fifteen loci, among them language, sensation, habitual imprint, the moistened seed, uninterrupted cessation, the object, the faculties, action, human effort, genuine insight, conformity, differentiated capacity, harmony, obstruction, and non-obstruction. Master Cháng Bǎi on the first: "In a single day one speaks at least hundreds, even thousands, of sentences, which unknowingly shape one's emotions, mindset, and fate."

subs.head: Ten causes, four conditions, five results

blocks.text: The **ten causes**: designation, correlation, impelling, generation, inclusion, drawing-forth, fixed distinction, concomitant action, opposition, and non-opposition. (This list is the *Yogācārabhūmi*'s own; the *Abhidharmakośa* has six causes.)

The **five results**: the ripened result, the result of equal outflow, the result of release from bondage, the result of human effort, and the dominant result. Master Cháng Bǎi: ordinarily "cause" is the main factor and "condition" the helping one.

**The cause of designation** (隨說因) rests on language: "a name is designated first, and thought proceeds from it; thought comes first, and speech proceeds from it; and by means of speech, all manner of verbal expression arises in accordance with what is seen, heard, sensed, and known." Names shape thought, thought shapes speech. This is Day 7's "linguistic seeds" seen from the other side.

**The cause of correlation** (觀待因) rests on sensation: looking to this in relation to that. Master Cháng Bǎi: "When hungry, one thinks of food." Those who want pleasure seek its means; those who do not want suffering seek to avoid its causes. He describes three levels of not wanting suffering: avoiding the lower realms leads to human or heavenly rebirth; avoiding the desire realm, to higher meditation; ultimately, avoiding the three realms, to the path beyond them.

**The cause of impelling** (牽引因) rests on habitual imprint: pure and impure karma "perfumes the formations of the three realms, and thereby impels a desirable or undesirable body". By the same force, "the external material world itself flourishes or declines". Here Day 8's shared karma of the world is given its technical name.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through which four gateways is cause-condition-result establishment presented?
options: ten causes, four conditions, five results, seven marks
through their marks, loci, differences, and establishment
quiz.why: "First, through their marks; second, through their loci; third, through their differences; fourth, through their establishment." §26–30 cover the marks, §31 the fifteen loci, §32 the differences (ten causes, four conditions, five results), and §33 on the establishment. C names outcomes within the "marks."

quiz.q: The inner power includes "having obtained a human body." According to Master Cháng Bǎi, why are humans best placed to practise?
options: hell is too painful, desire heavens too pleasant, form-realm gods too proud; humans excel in pure conduct, memory, and courage
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Hell is too painful, desire heavens too pleasant, form-realm gods too proud to be persuaded"; "so humans are best — they excel in pure conduct, memory, and courage." Venerable Miào Jìng: only in the human world is there "neither the lower realms' torment nor the gods' pleasure." Cháng Bǎi also tells of Upagupta seeing in meditation that a man had killed his mother and could not attain the path in this life — the opposite of being free of karmic obstruction.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT among this treatise's ten causes?
quiz.why: The ten: designation, correlation, impelling, generation, inclusion, drawing-forth, fixed distinction, concomitant action, opposition, and non-opposition. The "ripening cause" belongs to the *Abhidharmakośa*'s six causes, not this list; here "ripened" appears among the five results.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are the five results?
options: ripened, equal outflow, release from bondage, human effort, dominant
quiz.why: "The five results are: first, the ripened result; second, the result of equal outflow; third, the result of release from bondage; fourth, the result of human effort; fifth, the dominant result." The four conditions are causal, uninterrupted, object, and dominant. §43 ties each result to its loci.

quiz.q: The cause of designation rests on language. In what order do name, thought, and speech arise?
options: a name is designated first and thought follows; thought comes first and speech follows; through speech come expressions according to what is seen, heard, sensed, and known
quiz.why: "A name is designated first, and thought proceeds from it; thought comes first, and speech proceeds from it; and by means of speech, all manner of verbal expression arises in accordance with what is seen, heard, sensed, or known." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Once the name 'teacup' is set up, the mind can picture a teacup — that is thought." Both defiled and pure matters have this cause — naming the four foundations of mindfulness or the eightfold path is its pure form.

quiz.q: The cause of correlation rests on sensation. What simple example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: when hungry, one thinks of eating — hunger is the correlating cause of food
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Looking to that in relation to this is correlation — when hungry, one thinks of food; hunger is the correlating cause of eating." The text: those who seek desire-realm pleasure, in relation to it, "either seek to obtain, or to accumulate, or to make use of" its requisites.

quiz.q: On what locus does the cause of impelling rest, and what else does it affect?
options: habitual imprint — pure and impure karma perfumes the formations and impels desirable or undesirable bodies; by this dominant force, the external world flourishes or declines
quiz.why: "Pure and impure karma perfumes the formations of the three realms, and thereby impels a desirable or undesirable body … Further, by this same dominant force, the external material world itself flourishes or declines." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Habitual imprint is a habitual aura — chiefly, seeds"; the impelling cause "also acts as a dominant condition on the rise and fall of the external world." (The translation renders 諸行 as "formations" in one sentence and "the five aggregates' activity" in the next — logged in the correction list.)
